doc.title: Sherrie Maricle interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 18, 2001 [interview 1 of 2]

chapter: Growing up in Endicott and learning drums
title: Being the girl drummer in the school band
summary: She was an oddity as a serious female drummer, as were many women in her band later, and her friends in music were boys.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: Were you something of a — I don’t want to, don’t take this personal, an oddity in your school, being the girl stage band drummer? Was that kind of like strange?

I don’t mean that in a conceited way but I took it really seriously since I knew that’s what I wanted to do for a living, I was maybe more serious than other girls who were in the band playing other instruments. I think like a lot of the women in my band have had similar experiences. They were very dedicated and very serious at a pretty young age. You know I’m pretty passionate about it so that, it wasn’t weird with my other friends who were interested in pursuing the same thing, but they were all boys.
